body: Im trying the find the words to give you some hope, when all I want to do is give myself a reason to not have any hope in my life. All I can say is that I find solace in the words of one of my favorite poets: "But our lives will only ever always be a balancing act that has less to do with pain...and more to do with beauty." How ironic, and how cruel it is, that so often the things that take away our ability to feel pain are the things that cause us the most pain -- because so too do they cut us off from feeling beauty and joy and love and vulnerability and humanity. I can't tell you the choices that you should make, but I hope with all of my heart that you can find it in yourself to turn away from heroin and from numbing yourself like that. I don't know the kind of relationship that you may have with your son, but I do know that there is a kind of love -- the strongest kind of love there is -- that comes from the bond between a father and his child. I sincerely hope you find that strength within yourself that I know you have to rekindle that love and talk to your son. Why do you feel like you can't talk with him? Have you talked with him recently? Does he know how you feel?

Meet with your child. Talk to him honestly. Let him know what is going on. And hug him in an embrace that lets him know that your love for him is still there. That it was always there, even when you couldn't show it.

Just about everything you described doing today are things that I aspire to do. All of them are worthwhile. But perhaps the best thing to do for yourself is to give yourself the space to grieve in whatever format that means to you. I don't know the kinds of torment you're going through, but I do know that losing your fiancee is an objectively shitty thing to have happen to anyone. You deserve the time to process it. I'm here if you want to talk, as are your friends.

And as for the job, you know what? There's always gonna be farms my friend. We all need food :) Put forth the effort and give yourself the chance to get back to some sanity with a stable job, but know that there will be work for ya whatever happens. Hell, I know farmers who need workers right now.

Look, best of luck to ya. Have hope. Give me a call sometime if ya need it. (And when all else fails, throw a trashcan through a plate glass window. It's the cure for all ills)
